result:
Solution 3 is the only one I accept; Solutions 1 and 2 reject because their indices are too large.

**Solutions 1 and 2.** Solution 1 treats C_q as if it had the same index as C, but C_q is not linearly normal, so the index d−3 of the elliptic normal curve does not carry over. Solution 2 claims the index drops by exactly 1, to d−4. Both values are too large, as the secant-plane obstruction below shows.

**Upper bound.** The k-th secant variety of an elliptic normal curve has dimension min(2k−1, d−1). A general point q therefore lies on a k-secant (k−1)-plane ⟨D⟩ once k ≥ ⌈d/2⌉. Projecting from q sends this plane to a (k−2)-plane meeting C_q in a scheme of length k. By the Eisenbud–Green–Hulek–Popescu restriction theorem, property N_{2,p} forbids a (p+2)-secant p-plane. Taking p = k−2 with k = ⌈d/2⌉ shows N_{2,p} fails at p = ⌈d/2⌉−2. So the index is at most ⌈d/2⌉−3, which already contradicts d−3 and d−4 for d ≥ 7.

**Sharpness.** I did not prove that this is the only obstruction. I rely on my recollection, not fully certain, that the literature on syzygies of projections of elliptic normal curves gives exactly ⌈d/2⌉−3. Solution 3's sharpness argument is only a sketch, but its answer matches that recollection.

VERDICT 1: REJECT
VERDICT 2: REJECT
VERDICT 3: ACCEPT
